:::{#exm-fitting-procedure}
#### Inputs of two fitting procedures

Least-squares polynomial fitting of degree $\polydeg$ has these inputs:

- model family: the polynomials of degree at most $\polydeg$;
- objective function: the sum of squared errors over the training set;
- optimization algorithm: solving the normal equations, which finds the unique minimizer exactly;
- random seed: none, since nothing is random;
- tuning parameter: the degree $\polydeg$;
- preprocessing: none.

Because the minimizer is unique and exact, the family, the training set and the objective already determine the fitted rule.

A random forest of regression trees is different:

- model family: averages of regression trees;
- objective function: the sum of squared errors within each tree's leaves;
- optimization algorithm: greedy splitting of the covariate space, tree by tree;
- random seed: fixes which observations and covariates each tree uses;
- tuning parameters: the number of trees and the minimum leaf size;
- preprocessing: none.

Here the greedy search finds no exact minimizer,
so two seeds give different fitted rules from the same data.

:::
